title: Inspire Science: Physics (Inspire Physics), Student Edition

sources.what: publisher scope and sequence (units and modules)
district-hosted publisher program walkthrough (module numbers, Unit 2 storyline, sample lesson)
publisher product page (ISBN, copyright 2020, program scope)

summary: An NGSS-aligned high-school physics course descended from Glencoe's Physics: Principles and Problems, organised as a toolkit module plus six units of modules, each with a launch, several 5E lessons, and a wrap-up. It runs from one- and two-dimensional mechanics through momentum and energy, waves and light, electricity and magnetism, to quantum, solid-state, and nuclear physics.

toc.label: Module 1
toc.title: A Physics Toolkit
toc.covers: Scientific methods, SI units and measurement, precision and accuracy, and graphing data to build models.

toc.label: Unit 1
toc.title: Mechanics in One Dimension
toc.covers: Describing straight-line motion and explaining it with forces and Newton's laws.

children.label: Module 2
children.title: Representing Motion
children.covers: Motion diagrams, the particle model, coordinate systems, position-time graphs, and velocity.

children.label: Module 3
children.title: Accelerated Motion
children.covers: Acceleration, velocity-time graphs, the kinematic equations, and free fall.

children.label: Module 4
children.title: Forces in One Dimension
children.covers: Net force, Newton's three laws, weight, drag, tension, and interaction pairs.

toc.label: Unit 2
toc.title: Mechanics in Two Dimensions
toc.covers: How forces produce motion in a plane: vectors, projectiles, circular motion, gravitation, and rotation.

children.label: Module 5
children.title: Displacement and Force in Two Dimensions
children.covers: Adding force vectors in two dimensions, friction, and motion on inclined planes (Lesson 1 is 'Vectors').

children.label: Module 6
children.title: Motion in Two Dimensions
children.covers: Projectile paths shaped by gravity and drag, and centripetal force in circular motion.

children.label: Module 7
children.title: Gravitation
children.covers: The gravitational force that makes objects fall and holds planets and satellites in orbit.

children.label: Module 8
children.title: Rotational Motion
children.covers: How forces produce changes in rotation.

toc.label: Unit 3
toc.title: Momentum and Energy
toc.covers: Conservation laws for momentum and energy, thermal energy, and the behaviour of fluids and solids.

children.label: Module 9
children.title: Momentum and Its Conservation
children.covers: Impulse, momentum, and conservation of momentum in collisions and explosions.

children.label: Module 10
children.title: Energy and Its Conservation
children.covers: Work, power, kinetic and potential energy, and conservation of energy in collisions.

children.label: Module 11
children.title: Thermal Energy
children.covers: Temperature, heat, specific heat, changes of state, and the laws of thermodynamics.

children.label: Module 12
children.title: States of Matter
children.covers: Fluids and pressure, Pascal's, Archimedes', and Bernoulli's principles, and properties of solids such as thermal expansion.

toc.label: Unit 4
toc.title: Waves and Light
toc.covers: Oscillations and mechanical waves, sound, and the behaviour of light.

children.label: Module 13
children.title: Vibrations and Waves
children.covers: Periodic motion of springs and pendulums, wave properties, and wave behaviour at boundaries.

children.label: Module 14
children.title: Sound
children.covers: Sound waves, pitch and loudness, the Doppler effect, resonance, and musical sound.

children.label: Module 15
children.title: Fundamentals of Light
children.covers: Illumination, the speed of light, colour, polarisation, and the wave model of light.

children.label: Module 16
children.title: Reflection and Refraction
children.covers: Mirrors, Snell's law, total internal reflection, and lenses.

children.label: Module 17
children.title: Interference and Diffraction
children.covers: Double-slit and thin-film interference, diffraction gratings, and resolution.

toc.label: Unit 5
toc.title: Electricity and Magnetism
toc.covers: Electric charge and fields, circuits, magnetic fields, and electromagnetic induction.

children.label: Module 18
children.title: Electrostatics
children.covers: Charge, conductors and insulators, Coulomb's law, electric fields, potential difference, and capacitance.

children.label: Module 19
children.title: Electric Current and Circuits
children.covers: Current, resistance, Ohm's law, electric power, and series and parallel circuits.

children.label: Module 20
children.title: Magnetic Fields
children.covers: Magnets, fields produced by currents, and forces on currents and moving charges.

children.label: Module 21
children.title: Electromagnetism
children.covers: Electromagnetic induction, generators, transformers, and electromagnetic waves.

toc.label: Unit 6
toc.title: Subatomic Physics
toc.covers: Quantum behaviour of light and atoms, semiconductors, and the nucleus and elementary particles.

children.label: Module 22
children.title: Quantum Theory and the Atom
children.covers: The photoelectric effect, photons, atomic spectra, the Bohr model, and the quantum model of the atom.

children.label: Module 23
children.title: Solid State Electronics
children.covers: Conduction in solids, semiconductors, diodes, and transistors.

children.label: Module 24
children.title: Nuclear and Particle Physics
children.covers: Nuclear structure, radioactive decay, fission and fusion, and the Standard Model of particles.

notes: Module and unit titles are from the publisher's scope and sequence. Module numbers 5-8 are printed in the walkthrough; the others are numbered by position (Toolkit = 1) and should be checked against the book. Lesson titles were not found except Module 5, Lesson 1 'Vectors'. Each module has a launch, three or four lessons, and a wrap-up, and the walkthrough shows optional Earth and Space Science content linked to each unit.
